texts.preamble: M/S Shalimar Flour Mills & Anr vs Ut Of J&K & Anr on 6 March, 2023 Author: Sanjay Dhar Bench: Sanjay Dhar Sr. No.7 High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh At Jammu Crm(M) No. 179/2023 M/s Shalimar Flour Mills & Anr. ..... Petitioner(s) Through: - Mr. Ashwari Khajuria, Advocate Vs. Ut of J&K & Anr. ...Respondent(S) Through: - None Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sanjay Dhar, Judge Order 1) The petitioners have challenged the complaint filed by the respondents against them alleging commission of offences under Section 26 (2) (i) & (ii) read with Sections 59 (i) & 51 of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 filed before the Court of District Judicial Mobile Magistrate, Udhampur.
texts.facts: Order 1) The petitioners have challenged the complaint filed by the respondents against them alleging commission of offences under Section 26 (2) (i) & (ii) read with Sections 59 (i) & 51 of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 filed before the Court of District Judicial Mobile Magistrate, Udhampur. 2) It appears that the respondents have filed a complaint against the petitioners before the learned trial Magistrate alleging therein that on 01.08.2019, during routine inspection, the Food Safety Officer inspected the premises of petitioner No. 1/accused at Udhampur. Sample of wheat (2 kgs.) was lifted from the premises by the Food Safety Officer and the same was sealed. The sample was sent for analysis to the Food Analyst, Public Health Laboratory, Jammu. 3) As per report of the Food Analyst dated 06.08.2019, it was found that the sample did not conform to the standards prescribed for wheat falling under Regulation No. 2.4.6 (2) of Food Safety Standards (Food Products and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011 with respect to moisture, foreign matters, damaged grains and it contained large number of hairs and rats faecal matter. Accordingly, the sample was termed 'unsafe' and 'sub-standard'. After completing the legal formalities, the impugned complaint came to be filed by the respondents against the petitioners herein. 4) Heard and considered. M/S Shalimar Flour Mills & Anr vs Ut Of J&K & Anr on 6 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34107808/ 1 5)
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that the petitioners are getting the supply of wheat from the Consumer Affairs & Public Distribution Department of Jammu and Kashmir Government for grinding in the mills. It is submitted that the petitioners do not get the supply of wheat for grinding purpose from any other source. In this regard, the petitioners have relied upon agreement dated 20th of September 2013 executed between the CAPD Department of Jammu and Kashmir Government and the petitioners, a copy whereof has been placed on record. On this ground, it is urged that if at all the sample was found to be of sub-standard quality, the petitioners cannot be subjected to prosecution and it is the supplier of the wheat, who is to be prosecuted for the said purpose.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that the petitioners are getting the supply of wheat from the Consumer Affairs & Public Distribution Department of Jammu and Kashmir Government for grinding in the mills. It is submitted that the petitioners do not get the supply of wheat for grinding purpose from any other source. In this regard, the petitioners have relied upon agreement dated 20th of September 2013 executed between the CAPD Department of Jammu and Kashmir Government and the petitioners, a copy whereof has been placed on record. On this ground, it is urged that if at all the sample was found to be of sub-standard quality, the petitioners cannot be subjected to prosecution and it is the supplier of the wheat, who is to be prosecuted for the said purpose.
